small_guidance:
- The conv (8→64 ch, 3x3, 128x128 input, batch 128) dominates runtime; the fused LSE kernel is already cheap. Focus tuning on adding a custom conv kernel rather than further sweeping BLOCK_S/num_warps on the LSE kernel.
- For the existing fused_lse_kernel, try smaller BLOCK_S configs (64, 128) with num_warps=2/4 since the per-program work scans all 64 channels — smaller tiles give more parallelism across the (N, S/BLOCK_S) grid on 16128 spatial elements.
- Merge groupnorm_stats into a single persistent kernel per (N, group) that also writes a pre-normalized scratch, or better: pass `a, b` per (N, C) precomputed on the host so the LSE kernel does one load per channel of scale/shift instead of two loads + arithmetic.
large_guidance:
- Replace `self.conv` with a custom Triton conv2d kernel: im2col-style GEMM with one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile). With in_channels=8, kernel_size=3, the K dimension is only 72 — use BLOCK_K=72 (single iteration), BLOCK_M (OC)=64, BLOCK_N (spatial)=64/128. Fold conv bias into the epilogue.
- Go further and fuse conv → groupnorm-stats → normalize → tanh → hardswish → residual → LSE into a two-pass pipeline: pass 1 computes conv output into a scratch and per-(N,group) stats; pass 2 re-reads conv scratch, applies affine + activations + residual, and does the channel-wise LSE. Avoid materializing the post-activation tensor.
- Alternative: since channels=64 fits in registers, use a persistent per-(N, spatial_tile) kernel that computes conv for all 64 OC at once (accumulator [BLOCK_N, 64]), computes group stats across the tile contribution via a separate first pass, then in the second pass recomputes conv (or reads scratch) and immediately does normalize/activation/residual/LSE — keeping all channel values in registers for the LSE reduction.
